newsitem.title: UK: Ohio bids for DHL to relocate U.S. hub.
newsitem.headline: Ohio bids for DHL to relocate U.S. hub.

text.p: The state of Ohio is offering DHL a multi-million dollar incentive package to transfer its U.S. hub to the all cargo Rickenbacker airport, said Rickenbacker Port Authority executive director Bruce Miller.
"They (international air express company DHL) currently have their U.S. hub at Cincinnati, north Kentucky, where they have 44 to 45 flights in and out each night," he told Reuters in an interview.
"But DHL has made it known it needs a larger facility, its own 200-acre site, to handle its future growth and has approached us, and other candidates, to bid for this role," he said.
Miller added that the inducements being offered to DHL included rental payment offsetting, incentive financial contributions from Ohio state and local government and issuing DHL tax-exempt bonds.
He declined to disclose the amount on offer but said it would amount to "millions of dollars".
After sifting through 30 possible locations, Miller said DHL's other candidates were Cincinnati (a site opposite the present facility used by DHL), Dayton (Ohio) and Peoria (Illinois).
Industry sources said DHL will make a decision by the end of this year.
"If we get the vote then DHL will represent the cornerstone of Rickenbacker's future development," said Miller.
"DHL has told us it wants a 200-acre site. We currently have a 5,000-acre airport and, because we are blessed with plenty of land, we can expand to 20,000 acres," he said.
He added that Rickenbacker was a cargo only airport, catering for both commercial and military aircraft, had two 1,200-foot runways and was operational 24 hours a day.
Federal Express currently operates a 274,000 square-foot hub at Rickenbacker, one of seven it has in the U.S., noted Miller.
"The DHL site would be three times that size. And apart from FedEx and DHL, if we were to get that decision, we would also have the ability to handle a third major hub," he said.
Miller added he thought that Rickenbacker had "more than a reasonable chance" of securing the DHL U.S. operating hub contract.
"We are their type of airport...we are compatible with their needs," he said.

He also said that Rickenbacker would be stepping up its efforts to win more cargo traffic away from Chicago, New York and Atlanta airports, "all of which are just one day's trucking from our facility". - Reuters Air Cargo Service Tel +44 171 542 7706 Fax +5017
